name: unpause_fix
description: Make the paused game resumable by polling a key that exists.
evidence: $26B5 reads INKEY -106, the BBC COPY key that beebjit maps to End, and only if it is down falls into the busy-wait at $26BC
$26BC reads INKEY -90 and loops until it reports pressed, so that key is the only way out of the pause
every confirmed INKEY number in this game fits N-1 = row*16 + col, which places -90 at column 9 row 5
column 9 of a BBC Model B keyboard carries only the four cursor keys and COPY, at rows 1, 2, 3, 7 and 6, so row 5 is not connected to any key and INKEY -90 can never report pressed
two recorded sessions confirm it: $26BC spun 643,444 and 92,436 times while $26C3, the instruction after the loop, never executed once
qualifications: the matrix formula is derived from ten confirmed values rather than from a datasheet, and the claim that column 9 carries only five keys is from knowledge of the Model B keyboard rather than measured here; both would have to be wrong for the original to be resumable
this changes original behaviour rather than restoring intended behaviour: what the author meant the resume key to be is unknown, because $A6 polls a matrix position with no key wired to it
the replacement is BBC f3, INKEY -116, reached from PC F3; its matrix position of row 7 column 3 sits consecutively with f1 and f2, which is what a function key row should look like
on some laptops a function key needs Fn held, which beebjit's own KEYS file notes

an earlier test appeared to show f3 failing, but that trace ended at cycle 200,000,000 while the session could run to 630,000,000, so a later resume would have been invisible to it. The player reports seeing it work
